V2G capability has considerable potential to support the energy transformation and to reduce the total cost of EV ownership. In July 2024, Energy Ministers agreed to a national Consumer Energy Resources Roadmap, available at energy.gov.au. Consumer Energy Resources (CER) are devices that generate or store electricity, including EVs. Priorities under the CER Roadmap include: • updating Australian Standard 4777 to remove barriers to V2G charging. • developing a strategy to identify commercial pathways for vehicle-to-everything, building on ARENA’s Driving the Nation program. • reviewing technical and regulatory frameworks to remove barriers for consumer adoption of V2G opportunities. • developing nationally consistent standards for interoperability, including to enable V2G and vehicle- to-home (V2H) technologies. Over the past year, considerable progress has been made under the Roadmap: • In August 2024, Standards Australia issued a revised standard (AS/NZS 4777.2:2020 and 2:2024) that removes a barrier to many distribution network service providers (DNSPs) accepting V2G chargers on their networks. • In February 2025, ARENA in partnership with the RACE for 2030 Cooperative Research Centre, published the National Roadmap for Bidirectional EV Charging in Australia.33 • In May 2025, a review of jurisdictional technical and regulatory frameworks to remove barriers for consumer adoption of V2G opportunities commenced. • From mid-August 2025, public consultations commenced on both nationally consistent standards for interoperability, including to enable V2G and V2H technologies, and the national technical regulatory framework that will set and enforce these standards. National Electric Vehicle Strategy 2024-25Page 20 Key Achievements Since its release in April 2023, the Strategy has supported an accelerated transition to EVs in Australia, driving nationwide momentum and EV uptake. The Strategy includes a commitment to collaborate across jurisdictions on six key areas including: • national standards • data sharing • EV affordability • remote and regional EV charging infrastructure • fleet procurement • education and awareness. These priority areas were identified and are being championed by the National Electric Vehicle Action Plan Implementation Group (Implementation Group) – which includes members from all jurisdictions. Implementation Group Progress The Minimum Operating Standards (the standards) provide direction for government-supported EV charging infrastructure projects starting on or after 1 January 2024. The standards help ensure that Australian EV drivers have access to a convenient, reliable, affordable, and equitable national charging network. The standards offer guidance on matters such as design, payment methods, customer service and availability (uptime). The standards were developed in collaboration with Australian states and territories through the Implementation Group and were agreed to by the Energy and Climate Change Ministerial Council in November 2023. The Implementation Group has recently completed its first review of the standards, with particular focus on technological and regulatory progress. This process involved targeted public consultation, including with Distributed Network Service Provide (DNSPs), Charge Point Operators (CPOs), peak bodies, EV advocacy groups and other charging infrastructure experts. Various, and sometimes differing, views were provided. However, it was established that the standards remain broadly fit for purpose. Minor changes have been agreed to by the Implementation Group. The updated standards can be found on DCCEEW’s website. The standards will continue to be reviewed regularly to ensure they keep up with regulatory and technological progress. On 19 July 2024, Energy and Climate Change Ministers agreed to a national statement of intent for regional and remote EV charging infrastructure. The statement demonstrates governments’ commitment to working together to achieve effective planning, coordination and delivery of EV charging infrastructure nationally and to ensure regional and remote populations have access to reliable EV charging infrastructure, where practical. A National EV Charging Infrastructure Mapping Tool (EVCI Mapping Tool) has been developed with the support of the Implementation Group. The EVCI Mapping Tool includes the location of DC fast charging infrastructure (over 25kW capacity) across more than 16 Charge Point Operators (CPOs). The EVCI Mapping Tool has identified optimal zones to guide the deployment of fast EV charging, across all jurisdictions in Australia, based on a range of technical, social and economic considerations including (but not limited to) projected EV adoption and traffic movements. The EVCI Mapping Tool will support a more targeted and coordinated deployment of fast EV charging across Australia. Australia’s first National Electric Vehicle Strategy to drive cleaner, cheaper to run vehicles | Ministers for the Department of Infrastructure Skip to main content Ministers C King Wells Burke M King McBain Chisholm Green search rss Enter search terms The Hon Catherine King MP Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government C King Menu Close Biography Media releases Transcripts Speeches Communiques Contact Home The Hon Catherine King MP Media releases Australia’s first National Electric Vehicle Strategy to drive cleaner, cheaper to run vehicles Listen Australia’s first National Electric Vehicle Strategy to drive cleaner, cheaper to run vehicles The Albanese Government is today releasing Australia’s first National Electric Vehicle Strategy – a comprehensive roadmap to ensure Australians have a better choice of electric vehicles, and encourage greater use of cleaner, cheaper-to-run vehicles. As part of the Strategy and following extensive public consultation, the Government will introduce a Fuel Efficiency Standard, working with industry and the community to finalise details in coming months. Fuel efficiency standards are standards which outline how much pollution – or specifically, carbon dioxide – a car will produce when it’s running.  More efficient vehicles will produce fewer emissions – meaning their environmental impact is lower, and they are cheaper for motorists to run. Australia and Russia are among the only developed countries that don’t have fuel efficiency standards. The absence of a standard has meant Australians households and businesses are missing out on greater choice of car models and paying more in fuel costs to run their cars because manufacturers prioritise sending more efficient vehicles to countries with standards in place. On average, new cars in Australia use 40 per cent more fuel than the European Union, 20 per cent more than the United States, and 15 per cent more than New Zealand. Previous analysis has shown that the introduction of a fuel efficiency standard could save motorists $519 per year in fuel costs. With passenger cars making up almost 10 per cent of Australia’s CO2 emissions, it is an important step to meet our emissions reduction targets. Fuel Efficiency Standards will only apply to new cars, and not retrospectively, so consumers will still be able to choose they vehicle they want to drive. Australia also lags far behind other countries in EV sales, with our uptake of EVs around four times lower than the global average. The Strategy also looks at reducing barriers to electric vehicle uptake, whether it be demand, supply or infrastructure, which is the critical planning that consumers have been crying out for. Transport is the third largest source of emissions in Australia. This Strategy will help cut our emissions by at least 3 million tonnes of carbon by 2030, and over 10 million tonnes to 2035. Minister for Climate Change and Energy Chris Bowen said Australian governments, car makers, motoring clubs, climate groups, businesses and unions were all on board with getting cleaner and cheaper cars to Australia  “This strategy delivers on our commitment to provide greater choice for Australians to drive cars that are cleaner and cheaper to run,” Minister Bowen said. This strategy provides the coordination and leadership to drive down costs and improve infrastructure so–that we get more affordable and accessible electric vehicles on the market. “The Government has already cut taxes on EVs through the Electric Car Discount, saving up to $11,000 a year on a $50,000 electric vehicle. Thanks to the Albanese Government’s leadership, two and half times more EVs are being sold this year than they were at this time last year. “Fuel-efficient and electric vehicles are cleaner and cheaper to run – today’s announcement is a win-win for motorists.” Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government, Catherine King said the government would introduce fuel efficiency standards that work for Australia’s market. “This strategy offers an historic opportunity to develop fuel efficiency standards that learn from international best practice, while recognising the unique needs of Australians. It will send a strong message to the global car industry that when it comes to transport technology, Australia will no longer settle for less,” Minister King said. “More than 85 percent of all cars sold in the world are subject to fuel efficiency standards. It’s time Australians were offered the same choice.” Consultation on the design of fuel efficiency standards begins today, and is available through www.cleanercars.gov.au . Following the consultation, the Government will release its proposed Fuel Efficiency Standard by the end of 2023. The National Electric Vehicle Strategy is available at https://www.dcceew.gov.au/energy/transport . Menu Search Electric cars exemption You don't need to pay fringe benefits tax (FBT) on eligible electric cars and associated car expenses. Last updated 1 April 2026 Print or Download Eligibility for electric cars exemption You don't pay FBT if you provide private use of an electric car that meets all the following conditions: The car is a zero or low emissions vehicle . The first time the car is both held and used is on or after 1 July 2022. The car is used by a current employee or their associates (such as family members). Luxury car tax  (LCT) has never been payable on the importation or sale of the car. Benefits provided under a salary packaging arrangement are included in the exemption. The private use of an eligible electric car, and the cost of fuel (including electricity) to charge it is exempt from FBT. However, the benefit is reportable . The government will complete a review into this exemption by mid-2027 to consider electric car take-up. We will provide an update when this review begins. If you're not eligible for the exemption, for example the vehicle doesn't meet the conditions of a zero or low emissions vehicle, you may need to pay fringe benefits tax for the private use of the car. See Cars and FBT for more information. Zero or low emissions vehicle A vehicle is a zero or low emissions vehicle if it satisfies both of these conditions: It is one of the following – a battery electric vehicle hydrogen fuel cell electric vehicle It is a car designed to carry a load of less than one tonne and fewer than 9 passengers (including the driver). Motorcycles and scooters are not cars for FBT purposes and don't qualify for the exemption, even if they are electric. Plug-in hybrid electric vehicles From 1 April 2025, a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle will not be considered a zero or low emissions vehicle under FBT law and isn't eligible for the electric cars exemption. However, you can continue to apply the electric car exemption in certain conditions . 'Held and used' the electric car The practical effect of this requirement is that the electric car must be used for the first time on or after 1 July 2022 – even if it was held before this date. An electric car is 'held' when it is: owned (includes cars acquired under hire-purchase arrangements) leased (or let on hire) otherwise made available by another entity. An electric car is considered 'used' when it is used or available for use by any entity or person. Example: exemption does not apply – car first used before 1 July 2022 Shelly purchases an electric car on 1 April 2022. She makes it available for the private use of her employee, Jack, from that date until 30 July 2022. On 1 August 2022, Shelly sells the electric car to ABC Co. ABC Co makes the car available for the private use of its employees from 1 August 2022. The first time the electric car was both held and used is before 1 July 2022. Therefore, any car fringe benefits are not exempt from FBT. End of example   Example: exemption applies – car first used from 1 July 2022 John ordered an electric car on 1 February 2022. The car was not subject to LCT. The car was delivered on 15 June 2022, at which time legal ownership passed to John. John first makes the car available for the private use of his employees on 5 July 2022. On 1 September 2023, John sells the electric car to XYZ Co. The new owner makes the car available for the private use of its employees from 1 September 2023. The electric car was: first held on 15 June 2022 – when John started owning it first used on 5 July 2022. The first time the electric car was both held and used was after 1 July 2022. Therefore, any car fringe benefits are exempt from FBT. End of example Determining if the car was subject to LCT To be eligible for the exemption, the value of the electric car must be below the LCT threshold for fuel efficient vehicles at the time it is first sold in a retail sale and in any subsequent sale. If you purchase an electric car second hand, you need to determine if it was subject to LCT at any time in the past. Example: exemption does not apply – car was subject to LCT GHI Co purchases a new electric car on 1 July 2022 from a car dealership in Australia. The car's GST-inclusive value is $85,000. The car doesn't meet the company’s needs, so on 31 July 2022 they sell the car to Kerry for $83,000. Kerry reviews all available ownership and sales documentation and checks the LCT threshold for fuel efficient vehicles on the ATO website. She determines that LCT would have been payable by the dealership when GHI Co purchased the electric car, as the value of the car was above the fuel-efficient vehicle LCT threshold for 2022–23. Any car fringe benefits arising from the private use of the car by Kerry’s employees will not be exempt from FBT, as the car was subject to LCT when first sold. End of example Associated car expenses The following car expenses are exempt from FBT if they are provided for an eligible electric car: registration insurance repairs or maintenance fuel, including the cost of electricity to charge electric cars . You may be able to reduce the FBT on any items that aren’t exempt car expenses, if the expenditure would have been deductible to the employee if they incurred it themselves. This is called the otherwise deductible rule . Home charging station A home charging station is not a car expense associated with providing a car fringe benefit for electric cars. However, it may be a property fringe benefit or an expense payment fringe benefit . Cost of electricity to charge electric cars How you work out the cost of electricity depends on the type of electric car you provide. It can be difficult to work out the cost of electricity when an employee charges an electric vehicle (EV), or plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) at home. This is because any electricity used to charge the electric car is combined with the total amount of electricity consumed by an employee's home and is unable to be separately identified and valued. To make it easier for you to calculate these electricity costs, you can choose to use the shortcut EV home charging rate if you're eligible . See Fringe benefits tax – rates and thresholds for the rate. Check that you’re using the right rate for the right financial year. Otherwise you can use actual expenses to determine your value. If you choose to use the EV home charging rate, you can't include commercial charging station costs unless you can accurately determine the percentage of the vehicle's total charge based on the type of charging location. Make sure you keep the necessary records to substantiate how you determined the cost of electricity used to charge the EV, or the cost of fuel including electricity used to charge and run the PHEV. For more information, see PCG 2024/2 Electric vehicle home charging rate-calculating electricity costs when a vehicle is charged at an employee's or individual's home . Example: home charging percentage can be accurately determined Bill's employer provides him with an eligible electric car for his private use. During the 2026–27 FBT year: the car generates a report detailing that Bill charged the electric car at home 75% of the time Bill travelled a total of 10,000 km. Bill's home charging kilometres can be determined by applying the home charging percentage of 75% to the 10,000 total kilometres travelled. His employer decides to use the EV home charging rate of 5.47 cents, as follows: 10,000 km × 75% = 7,500 km 7,500 km × 5.47 cents = $410.25. The component of the electricity expense for FBT purposes would be $410.25. Bill has also kept relevant records relating to commercial charging station costs so his employer can include these costs to calculate the remaining component of the electricity expense. End of example Reportable fringe benefits Although the private use of an eligible electric car, including the associated expenses, is exempt from FBT, it is still a reportable fringe benefit . This means, you will need to work out: the notional taxable value of the benefits associated with the private use of the exempt electric car whether the benefit amount needs to be reported. Electric vehicles and fringe benefits tax fact sheet For more information on the electric cars exemption, see our Electric vehicles and fringe benefits tax fact sheet . sections.md:
## Plain-Language Summary

The Agreement on the European Economic Area (the 'EEA Agreement') entered into force on 1 January 1994. Pursuant to Article 98 of the EEA Agreement, the EEA Joint Committee may decide to amend, inter alia, Annex II to the EEA Agreement.

Directive 2013/56/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council is to be incorporated into the EEA Agreement. Directive 2013/56/EU repeals Commission Decision 2009/603/EC, which has been incorporated into the EEA Agreement. Given the specific legal and factual situation in Liechtenstein, Article 17 of Directive 2006/66/EC is not to apply to Liechtenstein. Annex II to the EEA Agreement should therefore be amended accordingly, and the position of the Union within the EEA Joint Committee should be based on the attached draft Decision.

## Overview

This brief covers Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156 of 13 July 2015, which sets the position to be adopted, on behalf of the European Union, within the EEA Joint Committee concerning an amendment to Annex II (Technical regulations, standards, testing and certification) to the EEA Agreement, specifically incorporating Directive 2013/56/EU (batteries and accumulators). Published in the Official Journal of the European Union, L 187/24, 15.7.2015.

**Item type:** Council Decision (EU) | **Jurisdiction:** EU/EEA | **Legal basis:** Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Article 192(1) and Article 218(9); Council Regulation (EC) No 2894/94, Article 1(3).

## Timeline

| Date | Milestone |
|---|---|
| 1 January 1994 | EEA Agreement entered into force |
| 13 July 2015 | Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156 adopted at Brussels; entered into force same date per Article 2 |
| 15 July 2015 | Decision published in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 187/24) |

## Gaps

*Gaps in this brief, verified against the captured EUR-Lex text (267,932-character raw capture):*

[penalty_summary] No penalty provisions are specified in the captured Decision text; this is a Council internal-position Decision, not a substantive compliance instrument.

[primary_deadline] No compliance deadline is stated in the captured Decision text.

The attached draft EEA Joint Committee decision itself (referenced in Article 1 but not reproduced within this Decision's own text) was not captured or verified in this brief, so the actual EEA-side amendment text and its own entry-into-force/transposition terms are not confirmed here.

## Operational Relevance

*Operational implication:* This Decision only sets the EU's own negotiating position ahead of a corresponding EEA Joint Committee decision; it does not itself amend the EEA Agreement or create a compliance obligation. Once the corresponding EEA Joint Committee decision is adopted (not captured in this brief), the practical effect is that Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway become bound by the EU's batteries-and-accumulators Directive 2013/56/EU on the same terms as EU Member States, except for the stated Liechtenstein carve-out on Article 17 of Directive 2006/66/EC -- relevant to any operator tracking battery/accumulator compliance obligations across EEA-wide, not just EU, supply chains.

## Sources

| # | Title | Issuing Body | Type | URL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Council Decision (EU) 2015/1156 of 13 July 2015 on the position to be adopted, on behalf of the European Union, within the EEA Joint Committee concerning an amendment to Annex II to the EEA Agreement (Batteries and Accumulators) | Council of the European Union | Tier 1 -- Binding law (Official Journal) | https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:32015D1156 |

## Key Legal Provisions (Verbatim)

**Recital 1:** 'The Agreement on the European Economic Area ('the EEA Agreement') entered into force on 1 January 1994.'

**Recital 2:** 'Pursuant to Article 98 of the EEA Agreement, the EEA Joint Committee may decide to amend, inter alia, Annex II to the EEA Agreement.'

**Recital 3:** 'Directive 2013/56/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council ... is to be incorporated into the EEA Agreement.'

**Recital 4:** 'Directive 2013/56/EU repeals Commission Decision 2009/603/EC ..., which has been incorporated into the EEA Agreement.'

**Recital 5:** 'Given the specific legal and factual situation in Liechtenstein, Article 17 of Directive 2006/66/EC is not to apply to Liechtenstein.'

**Recital 6:** 'Annex II to the EEA Agreement should therefore be amended accordingly.'

**Recital 7:** 'The position of the Union within the EEA Joint Committee should be based on the attached draft Decision,'

**[jurisdictional_scope] Article 1:** 'The position to be adopted, on behalf of the Union, within the EEA Joint Committee on the proposed amendment to Annex II (Technical regulations, standards, testing and certification) to the EEA Agreement shall be based on the draft decision of the EEA Joint Committee attached to this Decision.'

**[effective_date] Article 2:** 'This Decision shall enter into force on the date of its adoption.'

**Signed:** 'Done at Brussels, 13 July 2015.' — For the Council, F. ETGEN, The President.

      <div class="eli-container">
         <div class="eli-main-title" id="tit_1">
            <p class="oj-doc-ti" id="d1e39-24-1">
            COUNCIL DECISION (EU) 2015/1156</p>
            <p class="oj-doc-ti">of 13 July 2015
         </p>
            <p class="oj-doc-ti">on the position to be adopted, on behalf of the European Union, within the EEA Joint Committee concerning an amendment to Annex II (Technical regulations, standards, testing and certification) to the EEA Agreement (Batteries and Accumulators)</p>
         </div>
         <div class="eli-subdivision" id="pbl_1">
            <p class="oj-normal">THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION,</p>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="cit_1">
               <p class="oj-normal">Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Article 192(1) and Article 218(9) thereof,</p>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="cit_2">
               <p class="oj-normal">Having regard to Council Regulation (EC) No 2894/94 of 28 November 1994 concerning arrangements for implementing the Agreement on the European Economic Area <a id="ntc1-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0001" href="#ntr1-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0001"
                     >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">1</span>)</a>, and in particular Article 1(3) thereof,</p>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="cit_3">
               <p class="oj-normal">Having regard to the proposal from the European Commission,</p>
            </div>
            <p class="oj-normal">Whereas:</p>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_1">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(1)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">The Agreement on the European Economic Area <a id="ntc2-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0002" href="#ntr2-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0002"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">2</span>)</a> (‘the EEA Agreement’) entered into force on 1 January 1994.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_2">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(2)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">Pursuant to Article 98 of the EEA Agreement, the EEA Joint Committee may decide to amend, inter alia, Annex II to the EEA Agreement.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_3">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(3)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">Directive 2013/56/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council <a id="ntc3-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0003" href="#ntr3-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0003"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">3</span>)</a> is to be incorporated into the EEA Agreement.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_4">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(4)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">Directive 2013/56/EU repeals Commission Decision 2009/603/EC <a id="ntc4-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0004" href="#ntr4-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0004"
                                 >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">4</span>)</a>, which has been incorporated into the EEA Agreement.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_5">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(5)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">Given the specific legal and factual situation in Liechtenstein, Article 17 of Directive 2006/66/EC is not to apply to Liechtenstein.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_6">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(6)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">Annex II to the EEA Agreement should therefore be amended accordingly.</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_7">
               <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                  <col width="4%"/>
                  <col width="96%"/>
                  <tbody>
                     <tr>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">(7)</p>
                        </td>
                        <td valign="top"  >
                           <p class="oj-normal">The position of the Union within the EEA Joint Committee should be based on the attached draft Decision,</p>
                        </td>
                     </tr>
                  </tbody>
               </table>
            </div>
            <p class="oj-normal">HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION:</p>
         </div>
         <div class="eli-subdivision" id="enc_1">
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_1">
               <p id="d1e151-24-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 1</p>
               <p class="oj-normal">The position to be adopted, on behalf of the Union, within the EEA Joint Committee on the proposed amendment to Annex II (Technical regulations, standards, testing and certification) to the EEA Agreement shall be based on the draft decision of the EEA Joint Committee attached to this Decision.</p>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_2">
               <p id="d1e156-24-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 2</p>
               <p class="oj-normal">This Decision shall enter into force on the date of its adoption.</p>
            </div>
         </div>
         <div class="eli-subdivision" id="fnp_1">
            <div class="oj-final">
               <p class="oj-normal">Done at Brussels, 13 July 2015.</p>
               <div class="oj-signatory">
                  <p class="oj-signatory">
                     <span class="oj-italic">For the Council</span>
                  </p>
                  <p class="oj-signatory">
                     <span class="oj-italic">The President</span>
                  </p>
                  <p class="oj-signatory">F. ETGEN
            </p>
               </div>
            </div>
         </div>
         <hr class="oj-note"/>
         <p class="oj-note">
            <a id="ntr1-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0001" href="#ntc1-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0001"
               >(<span class="oj-super">1</span>)</a>  
            <a href="./../../../legal-content/EN/AUTO/?uri=OJ:L:1994:305:TOC"
               >OJ L 305, 30.11.1994, p. 6</a>.</p>
         <p class="oj-note">
            <a id="ntr2-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0002" href="#ntc2-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0002"
               >(<span class="oj-super">2</span>)</a>  
            <a href="./../../../legal-content/EN/AUTO/?uri=OJ:L:1994:001:TOC"
               >OJ L 1, 3.1.1994, p. 3</a>.</p>
         <p class="oj-note">
            <a id="ntr3-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0003" href="#ntc3-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0003"
               >(<span class="oj-super">3</span>)</a>  Directive 2013/56/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 November 2013 amending Directive 2006/66/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on batteries and accumulators and waste batteries and accumulators as regards the placing on the market of portable batteries and accumulators containing cadmium intended for use in cordless power tools, and of button cells with low mercury content, and repealing Commission Decision 2009/603/EC (<a href="./../../../legal-content/EN/AUTO/?uri=OJ:L:2013:329:TOC"
               >OJ L 329, 10.12.2013, p. 5</a>).</p>
         <p class="oj-note">
            <a id="ntr4-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0004" href="#ntc4-L_2015187EN.01002401-E0004"
               >(<span class="oj-super">4</span>)</a>  Commission Decision 2009/603/EC of 5 August 2009 establishing requirements for registration of producers of batteries and accumulators in accordance with Directive 2006/66/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council (<a href="./../../../legal-content/EN/AUTO/?uri=OJ:L:2009:206:TOC"
               >OJ L 206, 8.8.2009, p. 13</a>).</p>
      </div>
      <hr class="oj-doc-sep"/>
      <div id="L_2015187EN.01002601">
         <div class="eli-container">
            <p class="oj-normal">DRAFT</p>
            <div class="eli-main-title" id="tit_1">
               <p class="oj-doc-ti" id="d1e36-26-1">DECISION OF THE EEA JOINT COMMITTEE No …/2015</p>
               <p class="oj-doc-ti">of</p>
               <p class="oj-doc-ti">amending Annex II (Technical regulations, standards, testing and certification) to the EEA Agreement</p>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="pbl_1">
               <p class="oj-normal">THE EEA JOINT COMMITTEE,</p>
               <div class="eli-subdivision" id="cit_1">
                  <p class="oj-normal">Having regard to the Agreement on the European Economic Area (‘the EEA Agreement’), and in particular Article 98 thereof,</p>
               </div>
               <p class="oj-normal">Whereas:</p>
               <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_1">
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">(1)</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">Directive 2013/56/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 November 2013 amending Directive 2006/66/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on batteries and accumulators and waste batteries and accumulators as regards the placing on the market of portable batteries and accumulators containing cadmium intended for use in cordless power tools, and of button cells with low mercury content, and repealing Commission Decision 2009/603/EC <a id="ntc1-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0001" href="#ntr1-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0001"
                                    >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">1</span>)</a> is to be incorporated into the EEA Agreement.</p>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
               </div>
               <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_2">
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">(2)</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">Directive 2013/56/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council repeals Commission Decision 2009/603/EC <a id="ntc2-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0002" href="#ntr2-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0002"
                                    >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">2</span>)</a>, which is incorporated into the EEA Agreement and which is consequently repealed under the EEA Agreement.</p>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
               </div>
               <div class="eli-subdivision" id="rct_3">
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">(3)</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">Annex II to the EEA Agreement should therefore be amended accordingly,</p>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
               </div>
               <p class="oj-normal">HAS ADOPTED THIS DECISION:</p>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="enc_1">
               <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_1">
                  <p id="d1e93-26-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 1</p>
                  <p class="oj-normal">Chapter XV of Annex II to the EEA Agreement shall be amended as follows:</p>
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">1.</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">The following is added in point 12x (Directive 2006/66/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council):</p>
                              <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                                 <col width="4%"/>
                                 <col width="96%"/>
                                 <tbody>
                                    <tr>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">‘—</p>
                                       </td>
                                       <td valign="top"  >
                                          <p class="oj-normal">
                                             <span class="oj-bold">32013 L 0056</span>: Directive 2013/56/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 November 2013 (<a href="./../../../legal-content/EN/AUTO/?uri=OJ:L:2013:329:TOC"
                                                >OJ L 329, 10.12.2013, p. 5</a>).</p>
                                       </td>
                                    </tr>
                                 </tbody>
                              </table>
                              <p class="oj-normal">The provisions of the Directive shall, for the purposes of this Agreement, be read with the following adaptation:</p>
                              <p class="oj-normal">Article 17 shall not apply to Liechtenstein.’
                           </p>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
                  <table width="100%" border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0">
                     <col width="4%"/>
                     <col width="96%"/>
                     <tbody>
                        <tr>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">2.</p>
                           </td>
                           <td valign="top"  >
                              <p class="oj-normal">The text of point 12zt (Commission Decision 2009/603/EC) shall be deleted.</p>
                           </td>
                        </tr>
                     </tbody>
                  </table>
               </div>
               <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_2">
                  <p id="d1e135-26-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 2</p>
                  <p class="oj-normal">The texts of Directive 2013/56/EU in the Icelandic and Norwegian languages, to be published in the EEA Supplement to the <span class="oj-italic">Official Journal of the European Union</span>, shall be authentic.</p>
               </div>
               <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_3">
                  <p id="d1e143-26-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 3</p>
                  <p class="oj-normal">This Decision shall enter into force on …, provided that all the notifications under Article 103(1) of the EEA Agreement have been made <a id="ntc*1-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0003" href="#ntr*1-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0003"
                        >(<span class="oj-super oj-note-tag">*1</span>)</a>.</p>
               </div>
               <div class="eli-subdivision" id="art_4">
                  <p id="d1e152-26-1" class="oj-ti-art">Article 4</p>
                  <p class="oj-normal">This Decision shall be published in the EEA Section of, and in the EEA Supplement to, the <span class="oj-italic">Official Journal of the European Union</span>.</p>
               </div>
            </div>
            <div class="eli-subdivision" id="fnp_1">
               <div class="oj-final">
                  <p class="oj-normal">Done at Brussels,.</p>
                  <div class="oj-signatory">
                     <p class="oj-signatory">
                        <span class="oj-italic">For the EEA Joint Committee</span>
                     </p>
                     <p class="oj-signatory">
                        <span class="oj-italic">The President</span>
                     </p>
                  </div>
                  <div class="oj-signatory">
                     <p class="oj-signatory">
                        <span class="oj-italic">The Secretaries</span>
                     </p>
                     <p class="oj-signatory">
                        <span class="oj-italic">to the EEA Joint Committee</span>
                     </p>
                  </div>
               </div>
            </div>
            <hr class="oj-note"/>
            <p class="oj-note">
               <a id="ntr1-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0001" href="#ntc1-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0001"
                  >(<span class="oj-super">1</span>)</a>  
            <a href="./../../../legal-content/EN/AUTO/?uri=OJ:L:2013:329:TOC"

            <p class="oj-note">
               <a id="ntr2-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0002" href="#ntc2-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0002"
                  >(<span class="oj-super">2</span>)</a>

               <a id="ntr*1-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0003" href="#ntc*1-L_2015187EN.01002601-E0003"

## Enforcement and Penalty Position (Required Slot)

**[penalty_summary]** GAP: the reviewed recitals, Sole Article, and closing clause set the Community position on Annex C, part II computer-monitor specifications and the phased dates for their replacement; none of them prescribe a penalty, fine, or sanction for any party, reviewed as of this authoring pass.

This brief covers 2009/789/EC: Commission Decision of 26 October 2009 determining the Community position for a decision of the management entities under the Agreement between the Government of the United States of America and the European Community on the coordination of energy-efficiency labelling programmes for office equipment on the revision of the computer monitor specifications in Annex C, part II, to the Agreement (CELEX 32009D0789).

**Coverage note:** This authoring pass reviewed the Decision's recitals on the Annex C, part II computer-monitor specification timetable, the Sole Article, and the closing clause as captured from EUR-Lex; it does not itemize the underlying draft decision specifications themselves, which are not reproduced in this Decision's own text.

## Notification and Why This Applies to the Workspace

Done at Brussels, 26 October 2009. *Source: Commission Decision 2009/789/EC, closing clause, EUR-Lex CELEX:32009D0789*

*Operational implication:* this Decision fixes the Community's (now EU's) negotiating position ahead of a joint US-EU management-entities decision revising the Annex C, part II computer-monitor energy-efficiency specifications under the bilateral Energy Star agreement for office equipment, phased by monitor diagonal screen size (below 30 inches from 30 October 2009; 30 to 60 inches inclusive from 30 January 2010). It does not itself change the specifications; the substantive specification content is set by the subsequent management-entities decision referenced but not reproduced here. Freight forwarders and shippers of IT/office-equipment display cargo covered by the US-EU Energy Star programme should track the referenced management-entities decision, not this position-setting act, for the operative specification change.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the text of the draft decision on computer-monitor specifications referenced in the Sole Article has not been reviewed in this authoring pass.

## Effective Date and Deadline (Required Slots)

**[effective_date]** As of 30 October 2009, the computer monitor specifications in Annex C, part II, should be repealed for computer monitors with diagonal screen sizes below 30 inches, and replaced by the specification annexed to this Decision. *Source: Commission Decision 2009/789/EC, recital 4, EUR-Lex CELEX:32009D0789*

As of 30 January 2010, the computer monitor specifications in Annex C, part II, should be repealed for computer monitors with diagonal screen sizes from 30 to 60 inches, inclusive, and replaced by the specification annexed to this Decision. *Source: Commission Decision 2009/789/EC, recital 5, EUR-Lex CELEX:32009D0789*

**[primary_deadline]** GAP: the reviewed recitals set the phased dates on which the Annex C, part II specifications are replaced for computer monitors of different diagonal screen sizes (see effective_date), and the Sole Article and closing clause set the Community's negotiating position and this Decision's own adoption date; none of them establish a compliance deadline for any external party (manufacturer, importer, or Member State) distinct from the specification-replacement dates above, reviewed as of this authoring pass. No entry-into-force clause for this Decision itself was found in the reviewed text.

## What the Decision Does

**[jurisdictional_scope]** The position to be adopted by the European Community for a decision by the management entities under the Agreement between the Government of the United States of America and the European Community on the coordination of energy-efficiency labelling programmes for office equipment on revising the computer specifications in Annex C, part II, to the Agreement shall be based on the attached draft decision. *Source: Commission Decision 2009/789/EC, Sole Article, EUR-Lex CELEX:32009D0789*

## Confirmed Timing

**[effective_date] FACT:** Article 2 states: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the day of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Article 2, EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** It was published as "OJ L 252, 19.9.2012, pp. 1–3." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, OJ citation, EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** Article 2 also states: "It shall apply from 10 December 2011." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Article 2, EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** Recital (7) explains the rationale for retroactive application: "For reasons of legal certainty, this Regulation should apply from 10 December 2011." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Recital (7), EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** The Regulation was "Done at Brussels, 18 September 2012" and signed for the Commission by President José Manuel Barroso. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, signature block, EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** The captured EUR-Lex page's own ELI metadata records this instrument's force status via the ELI property `eli:in_force`, whose resource value ends in the token `InForce-inForce` (an ELI ontology term indicating current in-force status), and no text elsewhere in the reviewed scope of this Regulation itself repeals or supersedes it. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, ELI metadata header, EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

## Enforcement

**[penalty_summary] GAP:** the reviewed text of this Regulation (Article 1, Article 2, the final clause, the signature block, the Recitals, and the reviewed portions of the Annex) sets out the subject matter, entry-into-force/application rules, and the specific Annex XVII amendment; none of the reviewed text prescribes a specific penalty, fine, or sanction for non-compliance. A full-text search of the entire captured EUR-Lex page for this instrument for the terms "penalt", "Penalt", and "sanction" returned no matches, as of this authoring pass.

**FACT:** Recital (8) records that "The measures provided for in this Regulation are in accordance with the opinion of the Committee established under Article 133 of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006", i.e. the REACH Committee comitology procedure used to adopt this amendment. *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Recital (8), EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

*Operational implication:* this Regulation's direct relevance to freight and logistics operators is narrow and indirect. It amends a single entry (entry 23, cadmium) in REACH Annex XVII, restricting cadmium and cadmium compounds in specified plastic materials, and applies retroactively from 10 December 2011; the compliance obligation falls on manufacturers, importers, and downstream users placing cadmium-containing plastic articles (e.g. PVC- or PUR-based components) on the EU market, per the general REACH framework, rather than on the transport leg itself. The Regulation's own reviewed text states no penalty regime of its own -- enforcement of REACH restrictions generally runs through Member State market-surveillance and REACH-enforcement authorities under the broader REACH framework, which lies outside the scope of this specific amending Regulation's reviewed text. Freight forwarders and customs brokers handling cadmium-containing plastic articles or components (e.g. PVC cable insulation, epoxy-resin parts) moving into the EU should confirm upstream REACH Annex XVII compliance from shippers/manufacturers as part of standard product-compliance due diligence, since this Regulation's restriction is directly applicable across all Member States without national transposition.

## What the Regulation Does

**FACT:** Article 1 provides that "Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 is amended in accordance with the Annex to this Regulation." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Article 1, EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** Recital (1) identifies the predecessor instrument as "Commission Regulation (EU) No 494/2011 of 20 May 2011 amending Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH) as regards Annex XVII (Cadmium)", which "modified the scope of the restriction on cadmium and cadmium compounds, introducing provisions applicable to brazing sticks and jewellery in accordance with the risk evaluation and the risk reduction strategies for cadmium and cadmium oxide." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Recital (1), EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** Recital (3) states that "Following the adoption of Regulation (EU) No 494/2011, the Commission was informed of uses of cadmium pigments in certain types of plastics materials, restricted for the first time by Regulation (EU) No 494/2011, where suitable alternatives to the use of cadmium compounds appear not to be available and for which, due to the exceptional circumstances of a limited consultation, further assessment is now appropriate." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Recital (3), EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** Recital (4) records that "The Council Resolution of 25 January 1988 calls for an overall strategy to combat environmental pollution by cadmium, including specific measures to restrict the use of cadmium and stimulate the development of further alternatives to the use of cadmium in pigments, stabilisers and plating, asking for limitation of the uses of cadmium to cases where suitable alternatives do not exist." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Recital (4), EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** Recital (6) states that "Until the restriction procedure is finalised, the restriction on the use of cadmium and its compounds should be limited to the types of plastic material listed in entry 23 of Annex XVII before the adoption of Regulation (EU) No 494/2011." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Recital (6), EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** The Annex's chapeau states: "In Annex XVII to Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006, the table setting out the designation of the substances, groups of substances and mixtures and the conditions of restriction is amended as follows." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Annex, EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** Annex amendment point (1) provides that "in the second column of entry 23, the first and second subparagraphs of paragraph 1 are replaced by the following", with the replacement text specifying that the substance "Shall not be used in mixtures and articles produced from the following synthetic organic polymers (hereafter referred to as plastic material)", beginning with "polymers or copolymers of vinyl chloride (PVC) [3904 10] [3904 21]" and "polyurethane (PUR) [3909 50]" among the listed types (full list not transcribed in this pass). *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Annex point (1), EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**FACT:** Annex amendment point (2) provides that "in the second column of entry 23, in paragraph 1 the following subparagraph is added" (added subparagraph text not transcribed in this pass). *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Annex point (2), EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**[jurisdictional_scope] FACT:** The Regulation's final clause states: "This Regulation shall be binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, final clause, EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

**Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012 of 18 September 2012** amending Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 of the European Parliament and of the Council on the Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals (REACH) as regards Annex XVII (Cadmium) (Text with EEA relevance). Adopted by the European Commission and signed at Brussels on 18 September 2012 by President José Manuel Barroso; published as OJ L 252, 19.9.2012, pp. 1–3 (CELEX 32012R0835).

It also reviewed the opening framing text of the Annex (the chapeau, and the headings of amendment points (1) and (2) to entry 23, second column, paragraph 1) down through the first two listed polymer types (PVC and PUR), and the page's own ELI metadata recording the instrument's in-force status. It did NOT transcribe the remaining plastic-material types and their bracketed customs/tariff codes in the amended entry 23 table, nor the full text of the new subparagraph added by Annex point (2), nor the content of the footnoted source citations for Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 and Regulation (EU) No 494/2011 themselves -- that annex-table and cross-reference detail is out of scope for this pass and is a gap.

## Deadline

**[primary_deadline] FACT:** Article 2 sets the Regulation's retroactive application date: "It shall apply from 10 December 2011." This is the date from which the amended cadmium restriction became legally applicable, distinct from the Regulation's own entry into force on the day of its OJ publication (see Confirmed Timing above); Recital (7) explains this retroactive effect is "for reasons of legal certainty." *Source: Commission Regulation (EU) No 835/2012, Article 2, EUR-Lex CELEX 32012R0835.*

sections.md:
This brief covers the Convention on long-range transboundary air pollution (CELEX 21979A1113(01)), the 1979 Geneva Convention negotiated under the UN Economic Commission for Europe and concluded on behalf of the (then) European Economic Community.

The brief is structured as a Regulatory Fact Document. Sections without grounded content from the source corpus are labeled as a gap rather than filled in. All claims are labelled FACT, ANALYSIS, or GAP per the provenance contract.

**Coverage note:** This authoring pass reviewed the Convention's full preamble and Articles 1-18 (definitions, fundamental principles, air-quality management, research/monitoring cooperation, ratification, entry into force, withdrawal, authentic texts) as captured from EUR-Lex. It does not itemize the Convention's later Protocols (e.g. the Sofia Protocol on nitrogen oxides, separately tracked in this corpus under CELEX 21993A0621(01)) or the EEC's own concluding Decision.

## Effective Date and Deadline (Required Slots)

**[effective_date]** The present Convention shall enter into force on the 90th day after the date of deposit of the 24th instrument of ratification, acceptance, approval or accession. *Source: Convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, Article 16(1), EUR-Lex CELEX:21979A1113(01)* -- the Convention states this as a recurring threshold rule rather than a literal calendar date in its own operative text; EUR-Lex's own ELI metadata for this instrument records the resulting first date of entry into force, which is not itemized as a separate FACT here since it does not appear as prose in the reviewed operative text.

**[primary_deadline]** GAP: the reviewed Articles 1-18 lay down definitions, principles, cooperation mechanisms, and treaty-mechanics provisions (ratification, entry into force, withdrawal, authentic texts); none states a party-facing compliance deadline distinct from the Article 16 entry-into-force threshold, reviewed as of this authoring pass. Substantive emission-reduction deadlines were later introduced by this Convention's Protocols (e.g. the Sofia Protocol, CELEX 21993A0621(01)), not by the Convention itself.

## What the Convention Does

**[jurisdictional_scope]** "air pollution" means the introduction by man, directly or indirectly, of substances or energy into the air resulting in deleterious effects of such a nature as to endanger human health, harm living resources and ecosystems and material property and impair or interfere with amenities and other legitimate uses of the environment, and "air pollutants" shall be construed accordingly. *Source: Convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, Article 1(a), EUR-Lex CELEX:21979A1113(01)*

"long-range transboundary air pollution" means air pollution whose physical origin is situated wholly or in part within the area under the national jurisdiction of one State and which has adverse effects in the area under the jurisdiction of another State at such a distance that it is not generally possible to distinguish the contribution of individual emission sources or groups of sources. *Source: Convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, Article 1(b), EUR-Lex CELEX:21979A1113(01)*

The Contracting Parties, taking due account of the facts and problems involved, are determined to protect man and his environment against air pollution and shall endeavour to limit and, as far as possible, gradually reduce and prevent air pollution including long-range transboundary air pollution. *Source: Convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, Article 2, EUR-Lex CELEX:21979A1113(01)*

## Enforcement and Penalty Position (Required Slot)

**[penalty_summary]** GAP: the reviewed Articles 1-18 contain no penalty, fine, or sanction provision, reviewed as of this authoring pass. As a multilateral framework convention, its Article 17 mechanism for non-compliance by a Party is voluntary withdrawal (with five years' minimum standing and written notice) rather than a punitive measure.

## Why This Applies to the Workspace

At any time after five years from the date on which the present Convention has come into force with respect to a Contracting Party, that Contracting Party may withdraw from the Convention by giving written notification to the depositary. *Source: Convention on long-range transboundary air pollution, Article 17, EUR-Lex CELEX:21979A1113(01)*

*Operational implication:* this 1979 Convention is the foundational multilateral framework underlying decades of subsequent EU and international air-pollution and emissions policy relevant across all freight modes (vehicle/vessel/aircraft emissions, port and depot air-quality permitting, and transboundary pollutant monitoring). It sets no direct operational obligation on freight or logistics operators itself; live compliance obligations flow instead from its later Protocols and from EU secondary legislation implementing them, several of which are separately tracked in this corpus.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Convention's later Protocols, the EEC's own concluding Decision, and the specific ELI-metadata-recorded historical entry-into-force date have not been itemized as separate reviewed facts in this authoring pass.

sections.md:
**Who registers:** Chinese entities in covered sectors (power, steel, cement, aluminum, and others as expanded by MEE rules).
**What they report:** Verified annual emissions reports; authenticity, accuracy, and completeness are statutory obligations under Article 1037.
*Specific format for workspace Scope 3 data requests not available from primary sources as of June 2026.*
*Analytical inference:* The workspace should establish a contractual mechanism with Chinese ETS-covered counterparties to receive copies of verified annual emission reports for Scope 3 calculation purposes under EU CSRD or equivalent frameworks.

| Date | Event | What the Workspace Must Have Done |
|---|---|---|
| March 12, 2026 | Code adopted by 14th NPC. In force as of this date for legislative purposes. | Awareness. Begin compliance gap assessment. |
| April 30, 2026 | CSDS disclosure deadline for large Chinese listed companies (2025 financial year). | Collect available CSDS reports from listed Chinese shipper clients for Scope 3 baseline data. |
| August 15, 2026 | **Code enters force.** All 1,242 articles operative. Enforcement jurisdiction active. | EIA review complete for China-based facilities; chemical cargo compliance checkpoint operational; dual-penalty governance structures documented; China-facing staff trained. |
| H2 2026 | MEE and ministerial implementing regulations expected (chemical management, environmental monitoring, marine protection). | Monitor MEE publications; assess new obligations as regulations are published; re-check before end of 2026. |
| H2 2026 | Local legislature review of conflicting provincial environmental rules. | Re-verify compliance posture for any provincial-level rules relied upon in China-based operations. |
| 2026–2027 | Supreme People's Court / Procuratorate judicial interpretations on Code enforcement. | Monitor for interpretations affecting joint liability scope for supply chain participants. |
| 2027 | Anticipated ETS transition from intensity-based benchmarks to absolute emission caps. | Update Scope 3 modelling for Chinese ETS-covered clients; assess commercial implications for carbon-intensive freight. |
| 2026–2030 | 15th Five-Year Plan implementation period. Energy intensity reduction target: 17% CO₂/GDP by 2030. | Ongoing monitoring of sector-specific implementing regulations and zero-carbon corridor designations. |
| Post-2026 (date not confirmed) | Dedicated climate change law expected to be drafted. | Track NPCSC legislative planning announcements annually. |

**Penalty slot:** The Code's penalty provisions are operative from August 15, 2026. Chemical violation fines range from RMB 100,000 to RMB 2,000,000 depending on violation type and correction status (Articles 1205–1207). Dual penalties apply simultaneously to enterprises and responsible individuals under Part V. *Specific penalty provisions for ETS non-compliance not quantified in penalty summary as of June 2026 from primary sources;* the Code states consequences include "substantial fines and potential suspension of operations" but the exact ETS penalty schedule was not extracted verbatim from the source blocks. *Specific ETS penalty figure not available from primary sources as of June 2026.*

---

*Analytical inference:* **Statutory foundation (FACT):** Article 1037: "The State shall establish a national carbon emissions trading market. Key greenhouse gas emitting entities included in the national carbon emissions trading market shall fulfil their mandatory emission reduction responsibilities in accordance with national regulations." *Source: ClientEarth Asia, "China's new Environmental Code – how big of a deal is it?", March 17, 2026. https://www.clientearth.asia/latest/news/china-s-new-environmental-code-how-big-of-a-deal-is-it/

*Analytical inference:* **Data integrity requirement (FACT):** "Article 1037 of the Code that major greenhouse emitters are responsible for the authenticity, accuracy, and completeness of their emission statistics and annual emission reports." *Source: CCICED/ClientEarth, "How China's New Environmental Code Lays the Ground for 2060 Carbon Neutrality," March 25, 2026. https://cciced.eco/climate-governance/how-chinas-new-environmental-code-lays-the-ground-for-2060-carbon-neutrality-and-aligns-with-cciced-recommendations/

*Analytical inference:* **ETS sector coverage (FACT):** "The ETS expansion to steel, cement, and aluminum smelting (adding approximately 1,500 enterprises) was completed in 2024, raising total coverage to roughly 60% of China's GHG emissions." *Source: AllBright Law Offices, "China's Eco-Environment Code: Codifying the Green Transformation," April 30, 2026. https://www.allbrightlaw.com/EN/10531/177523769611f595.aspx

*Operational implication:* For workspaces with Chinese manufacturing clients in steel, cement, or aluminum — sectors common in industrial freight — those clients are now statutory ETS participants. Their annual verified emissions reports are legally mandated documents that the workspace may need to request for its own Scope 3 calculations.

*Analytical inference:* **MRV digitisation requirement (FACT):** "the Ecological Environment Monitoring Regulation (effective January 1, 2026) mandates automated, digitized environmental monitoring and establishes legal liability for data falsification." *Source: AllBright Law Offices, "China's Eco-Environment Code: Codifying the Green Transformation," April 30, 2026. https://www.allbrightlaw.com/EN/10531/177523769611f595.aspx

*Analytical inference:* This pre-existing digitisation mandate, now reinforced by the Code's enforcement framework, means that Chinese covered entities producing emissions data for the workspace's Scope 3 calculations are subject to legal liability for data inaccuracy. This increases (but does not guarantee) the reliability of that data compared to the prior voluntary disclosure environment.

*Status (FACT):* "the chapter on 'green and low carbon development' lays the foundation for a climate law, which is expected to be drafted in the coming years." *Source: ClientEarth Asia, "China's new Environmental Code – how big of a deal is it?", March 17, 2026. https://www.clientearth.asia/latest/news/china-s-new-environmental-code-how-big-of-a-deal-is-it/

*Analytical inference:* The Code's Part IV is explicitly designed as a legal placeholder until a dedicated climate law provides "much needed legal specificity." No published drafting schedule exists as of June 2026. The workspace should monitor NPCSC legislative planning announcements for inclusion of a climate law in the 15th NPC work programme.
*Re-check window:* Annual NPCSC legislative plan publications (typically March each year).

*Analytical inference:* *Status (FACT):* "Local legislature will also conduct a comprehensive review of local environmental laws and regulations. Provisions that conflict with the Code will be repealed or amended in line with the Code." *Source: ClientEarth Asia, "China's new Environmental Code – how big of a deal is it?", March 17, 2026. https://www.clientearth.asia/latest/news/china-s-new-environmental-code-how-big-of-a-deal-is-it/

*Operational implication:* Provincial-level environmental rules that currently apply to the workspace's China-based facilities may be amended or repealed. Compliance postures based on local regulations should be re-verified after August 15, 2026.

*Analytical inference:* *Status (FACT):* "A series of implementing regulations are also expected to follow, such as regulations on marine environmental protection, chemical management, environmental monitoring, etc., which would be drafted by the respective ministries." *Source: ClientEarth Asia, "China's new Environmental Code – how big of a deal is it?", March 17, 2026. https://www.clientearth.asia/latest/news/china-s-new-environmental-code-how-big-of-a-deal-is-it/

*Parties:* Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE), relevant sector ministries.
*Phase:* Announced intent; no published draft schedule as of June 2026.
*Analytical inference:* Implementing regulations for chemical management are of highest direct relevance to freight forwarders moving chemical cargo. MEE regulations on environmental monitoring will determine the technical standards for MRV data that Chinese ETS-covered shippers must meet.
*Re-check window:* Q4 2026 for first MEE implementing regulation publications.

## Q1: Does the Code directly regulate foreign freight forwarders operating in China?

**Status: Legal Confirmation Required.**
*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the Code's general enterprise obligations in Part I (including environmental impact obligations and the GHG reporting framework) apply to wholly foreign-owned enterprises (WFOEs) or foreign-invested entities operating logistics services within China, in the same manner as domestic enterprises, requires counsel review of the Code's jurisdictional scope provisions and China foreign investment law.

## Q2: Does the Code's ETS obligation cover road transport operators in China?

**Decided (partial):** The Code's ETS (Article 1037) currently covers "key greenhouse gas emitting entities" as defined under national regulations. *Analytical inference:* Road freight operators are not currently listed as covered sectors in published ETS rules (which cover power, steel, cement, aluminum, chemicals, paper, and aviation). Whether road freight will be added under implementing regulations is a research gap; no authoritative guidance has been published as of June 2026. The workspace should track MEE ETS sector expansion publications.

## Q3: Does the Code's EPR expansion to new energy vehicles affect the workspace?

**Status: Narrow applicability.** *Analytical inference:* EPR obligations for NEV manufacturers and battery producers do not directly apply to freight forwarders unless the workspace acts as importer of record for EVs or batteries into China. Workspaces handling automotive cargo on China import lanes should confirm the specific import-of-record role.

## Q4: Does the Code's dual penalty system apply to expatriate personnel?

**Status: Legal Confirmation Required.**
*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether the dual penalty provisions in Part V apply to expatriate managers or foreign nationals acting as legal representatives of Chinese-registered entities requires counsel review of the Code's enforcement scope and conflict-of-laws implications.

## Q5: Does the Code's new pollutant framework create cargo acceptance obligations for the workspace?

*Analytical inference:* **Decided (partial):** The Key Controlled New Pollutant List under Article 649 creates obligations for producers, importers, and users of listed substances. *Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether freight forwarders who accept, transport, or facilitate the import of goods containing listed substances are subject to direct obligations (rather than their shipper clients) under the Code requires counsel review.

---

*Analytical inference:* *Status (FACT):* "The Code's framework anticipates a transition from intensity-based benchmarks to absolute emission caps by 2027 — a structural shift that will significantly strengthen price signals for heavy industry." *Source: AllBright Law Offices, "China's Eco-Environment Code: Codifying the Green Transformation," April 30, 2026. https://www.allbrightlaw.com/EN/10531/177523769611f595.aspx

*Operational implication:* Chinese industrial shippers on the workspace's lanes that are ETS-covered entities will face a step-change in carbon cost exposure in 2027. *Analytical inference:* This is likely to increase demand for carbon-efficient logistics options and generate client conversations about Scope 3 emissions in freight specifically.
*Re-check window:* Q1 2027 for MEE ETS rule publication on cap methodology.

## EU CBAM Interaction

*Analytical inference:* The Code's carbon footprint measurement framework (Article 1036, CO₂-equivalent across all GHGs) and its statutory ETS MRV requirements create a structural alignment with EU CBAM's embedded emissions methodology. Chinese exporters of CBAM-covered goods (steel, cement, aluminum, fertilizers, electricity, hydrogen) who are also ETS-covered entities will now have statutory MRV data. However, CBAM's specific data verification and default value rules are determined by EU implementing regulation, not by the Code. Whether Chinese ETS data is directly usable for CBAM declarations is not resolved by either instrument and remains a research gap.

**No content for quantified cross-regulatory cost analysis as of June 2026:** The interaction between Chinese ETS carbon prices and EU CBAM certificate prices for the same emission units requires case-specific modelling that is not available from primary sources.

## 15th Five-Year Plan Alignment

*Analytical inference:* **Five-Year Plan carbon targets (FACT):** "The climate-related objectives are to achieve the goal of carbon peaking as scheduled, to reduce the carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP by 17% by 2030, and to build a clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient new energy system." *Source: Climate-Laws.org, "15th Five-Year Plan," 2026. https://climate-laws.org/document/14th-five-year-plan_0496

*Analytical inference:* **Zero-carbon infrastructure (FACT):** The 15th FYP calls for building "about 100 national zero-carbon parks to manufacture green products with green energy, with zero-carbon transportation corridors." *Source: Climate-Laws.org, "15th Five-Year Plan," 2026. https://climate-laws.org/document/14th-five-year-plan_0496

*Analytical inference:* The zero-carbon transportation corridors target in the 15th FYP is significant for road freight operators in China. *Analytical inference:* If the workspace operates or subcontracts road freight within designated zero-carbon corridors, it may face operational equipment requirements (electric vehicles, hydrogen vehicles) ahead of a national mandate. This is a directional signal, not a current compliance obligation.

## Dedicated Climate Law — Future Instrument

*Analytical inference:* The Code is explicitly designed as a legal placeholder for a dedicated climate change law expected "in the coming years." When that law is enacted, it is expected to provide "legal specificity around the key measures for China's continued decarbonisation" beyond what the Code's Part IV currently provides. The workspace should track NPCSC legislative planning for this instrument as it represents the highest-risk future regulatory event for carbon-intensive freight operations on China lanes.

---

*Analytical inference:* *Status (FACT):* "The main objectives of the 15th Five-Year Plan are listed in Chapter III. The climate-related objectives are to achieve the goal of carbon peaking as scheduled, to reduce the carbon dioxide emissions per unit of GDP by 17% by 2030, and to build a clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient new energy system." *Source: Climate-Laws.org, "15th Five-Year Plan," 2026. https://climate-laws.org/document/14th-five-year-plan_0496

*Analytical inference:* The 15th FYP's explicit energy intensity reduction target (17% CO₂ per unit GDP by 2030) creates a policy environment in which Chinese industrial counterparties face both statutory Code obligations and central government planning targets. The combination increases the probability that Chinese shippers will generate carbon performance requirements for logistics providers as part of their own supply chain emissions management.

---

*Status (FACT):* "The Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate might also release new judicial interpretations or guidance documents to ensure effective implementation of the Code." *Source: CCICED/ClientEarth, "How China's New Environmental Code Lays the Ground for 2060 Carbon Neutrality," March 25, 2026. https://cciced.eco/climate-governance/how-chinas-new-environmental-code-lays-the-ground-for-2060-carbon-neutrality-and-aligns-with-cciced-recommendations/

*What it will decide:* How liability provisions in Part V are applied to corporate entities and individuals; scope of public interest litigation standing; interpretation of joint liability for supply chain participants.
*What the workspace should expect to need to decide:* Whether individual managers in China-registered entities require personal environmental liability coverage or indemnity arrangements.
*Re-check window:* End of 2026.

为了保护生态环境，防治污染和其他公害，保障公众健康和生态环境权益，维护生态安全，推动绿色低碳发展，建设生态文明，全面推进美丽中国建设，加快推进人与自然和谐共生的现代化，实现中华民族永续发展，根据宪法，制定本法。 第二条 本法所称生态环境，是指影响人类生存和发展以及生态系统功能的各种天然的和经过人工改造的自然空间、自然因素及其相互联系与作用的总体，包括大气、水、海洋、土地、矿藏、森林、山岭、草原、湿地、冰川、高原、荒漠、野生生物、自然遗迹、人文遗迹、自然保护地、城市和乡村等。 第三条 中华人民共和国领域和中华人民共和国管辖的其他海域内的污染防治、生态保护、绿色低碳发展等生态环境保护相关活动，适用本法。 在中华人民共和国领域和中华人民共和国管辖的其他海域以外，造成或者可能造成中华人民共和国领域和中华人民共和国管辖的其他海域环境污染、生态破坏的，适用本法相关规定。 第四条 生态环境保护坚持中国共产党的领导，贯彻习近平生态文明思想，树立尊重自然、顺应自然、保护自然的生态文明理念，坚持良好生态环境是最普惠的民生福祉，完善落实绿水青山就是金山银山理念的体制机制，坚持用最严格制度最严密法治保护生态环境。 第五条 节约资源和保护生态环境是国家的基本国策。 国家采取有利于保护生态环境、促进人与自然和谐共生的经济、技术等政策措施，统筹产业结构调整、污染防治、生态保护、应对气候变化，协同推进降碳、减污、扩绿、增长，推进生态优先、节约集约和绿色低碳发展。 第六条 生态环境保护坚持预防为主、系统治理、生态优先、绿色发展、公众参与、损害担责的原则。 第七条 任何单位和个人都有保护生态环境的义务。 第八条 各级人民政府应当加强生态环境保护工作，正确处理高质量发展和高水平保护的关系，根据生态环境保护目标和治理任务，采取有效措施，改善生态环境质量。 地方各级人民政府应当对本行政区域及其管理的海域的生态环境保护工作和生态环境质量负责。 第九条 企业事业单位和其他生产经营者应当采取有效措施，防止、减少环境污染和生态破坏，节约集约利用资源，控制温室气体排放，履行绿色低碳发展义务，并对所造成的损害依法承担责任。 第十条 公民应当增强生态环境保护意识，采取简约适度、绿色低碳的生活方式，自觉履行生态环境保护义务，遵守生态环境法律法规，配合实施生态环境保护措施。 第十一条 国家支持生态环境科学技术研究、开发和应用，加强生态环境保护工作的科技支撑和人才培养，在确保安全前提下促进信息技术、数字技术、人工智能技术等的应用，提高生态环境保护的科学技术水平。 第十二条
